- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25) in the recent history, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior peak.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes; apply a 2–5 day lag correction for the first 5–7 days.
- After a price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 10–15% below the immediate peak for 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment neutrality (0.00) doesn’t imply no bias — model still tends to overforecast; apply a 1–3% downward bias if no sentiment signal is present.
- Horizon-specific: 1–3 day forecasts are often too optimistic; for 30-day, reduce forecast by 2–4% if recent 18-day average is >70.00.
